newsitem.title: INDONESIA: Indonesia late palm olein stable, interest thins.
newsitem.headline: Indonesia late palm olein stable, interest thins.

text.p: Indonesian palm olein prices were generally holding in late trading on Wednesday but interest waned following a softening in Malaysian values, traders said.
They said olein was around 1,360-65 rupiah/kg in Jakarta and 1,340 rupiah in the North Sumatran city of Medan.
"The market turned quiet after prices became weaker in Malaysia," one trader said. "Players are beginning to wonder if the (local) rebound is going to be short-lived."
Another trader said buyers were taking a wait and see position after the poor performance in Malaysia, hoping that local prices would follow suit.
Traders said news that state logistics agency BULOG would import crude palm oil ahead of the Moslem Ramadan fasting month in January confirmed their suspicions.
BULOG chief Beddu Amang said that the agency, which imported 20,000 tonnes of crude palm oil ealier this year, would continue to import but did not say how much or when.

One trader said supply seemed ample in Jakarta with about 100,000 tonnes of crude palm oil and palm products entering the capital in October. Data from Belawan Port showed that the MT Bobo-lV will leave the North Sumatran port for Singapore with 5,000 tonnes of crude palm oil on Thursday.
